newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Agan rated a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Agan rated a buy.

text.p: Israel's Agan Chemical Manufacturers Ltd is greatly undervalued, said Bank Hapoalim's securities department, which issued a buy recommendation for the share.
The bank said the company was valued at $300 million to $320 million against its present market valuation of $244 million.
Agan is trading at 50.76 shekels per share or a multiple of 9.4 times estimated 1996 earnings.

Hapoalim estimated the company's net profit at 81.3 million shekels or 5.39 shekels per share in 1996 and 90.6 million or 6.02 shekels per share in 1997 against 73.7 million or 4.89 shekels a share in 1995.
It forecast revenues would rise to 737 million shekels in 1996 and 854.9 million in 1997 from 671.1 million last year.
Agan is a subsidiary of Makteshim Chemical Works, itself a subsidiary of Israel's largest holding company, Koor Industries.

The Makhteshim-Agan group is the world's largest producer of generic agrochemicals. Koor plans to reorganise the two companies, which will be delisted in May and replaced by a new holding company called M.A.G.M. Chemistry Holdings.
